plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of silvery-green plants carry slender spikes of violet-blue flowers. They ripple across the Valensole plateau in Provence. The air is heavy with a sweet, herbal perfume, and the blooms hum with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with a peak in July
plants.funFact: Lavender is in the mint family. Its fragrant oils have been used for centuries to scent linens, soothe nerves and repel moths.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: In the depths of the Australian winter, this hardy tree puts on a show of fluffy, golden pom-pom flowers. They light up the bushland of the southeast with sunny color and a honey-sweet scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere (about June to August, with some blooming into September)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including South Australia and Victoria
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. They are a staple of summer borders and prairies. Butterflies and bees visit them all season, and goldfinches come for the seeds later on.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, from about June through August, with a strong July display
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, including the Midwestern United States
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek word for hedgehog. It refers to the prickly central cone of the flower head.
